title: Introduce lightweight CI warmup and dependency freshness index
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an opt-in lightweight CI warmup (toolcache + node_modules priming) and a dependency freshness index used to prioritize dep refresh churn. No API surface changes.
description: Summary: This PR adds a small, opt-in CI warmup step and a repository-level dependency freshness index. The warmup pre-populates frequently used caches (toolcache artifacts, node_modules cache, Docker layer primes) for long-running CI runners to reduce cold-start noise on presubmit and nightly lanes. The freshness index is a sampled metric computed from lockfiles and package metadata; it drives presubmit heuristics (which deps to pin, which paths should opt into fastpath) and feeds a lightweight dashboard. Motivation: We see intermittent presubmit flakiness and slow bootstraps caused by tool and devdep installs. Long tests amplify variance when runners start cold. Rather than making large CI images, this approach keeps images small and warms runners selectively, reducing median presubmit latency and lowering tokenized runner time. What changed (high level): - ci/warmup/: new script and small Go binary that runs in the CI runner init phase to prefetch toolcache (gcc, rustup, python wheels) and restore node_modules cache fragments. - ci/presubmit-config.yml: new opt-in warmup gate for selected jobs (lint, js-unit, e2e-smoke). - infra/dep-freshness/indexer.go: first pass indexer that computes a skyline freshness score per dependency by sampling package-lock/yarn.lock and direct devdep manifests. - web/telemetry/dep_freshness_exporter: exporter that pushes a compact index to our internal metrics; used by a dashboard in Console. - docs/ci-warmup.md and docs/dep-freshness.md: description, opt-in instructions, and troubleshooting. Rollout plan: feature flag (rdw.ci.warmup) behind which runners will execute warmup. We enable on a small set of nightly and presubmit lanes for core packages first, observe CI duration and flakiness for 1 week, then broaden. Performance expectations: warmup itself is ~20–70s depending on runner (primarily network bound) but reduces full job startup time by an estimated 15–35% for jobs that perform installs. Dependency freshness index is lightweight (run as a cron job) and will not affect presubmit runtime. Backwards compatibility: all changes are opt-in and non-breaking. The warmup script is skipped unless the job elects to run it. Testing done: - unit tests for indexer (go test) - integration harness run locally to simulate cache priming against a controlled registry - presubmit smoke job run on the canary pool (2 runs) - e2e-smoke run in staging after warmup gating Review notes: - Implementation intentionally keeps runtime tooling minimal (Go binary + shell adapters) to avoid large container images. - Index is conservatively tuned to focus on top-200 dependencies by reach; future PRs will expose more heuristics for devdep vs runtime pinning. - The exporter sends aggregated metrics only; no build artifacts or lockfile contents are exported. Known limitations & follow-ups: - Native build artifact priming (e.g., large prebuilt wheels) is intentionally limited for now; follow-up PR will add optional artifact priming for ruby/golang modules. - We currently support npm/yarn/pnpm and python pip; additional ecosystem support will be gated by usage. - A machine-learning driven warmup ordering could be added later, but initial rollout uses simple heuristics. Please see changed files for details and runbook in docs/ci-warmup.md for troubleshooting.

notes_for_maintainers: After merge: monitor 'ci.warmup.latency' and 'dep_freshness.top_changed' dashboards for the first 72 hours. If rollout shows higher flakiness, flip rdw.ci.warmup=false in infra/featureflags and revert the presubmit gate.
